key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Can be acute (trauma, rupture) or subacute (effusion accumulation). LOCATION: Chest (retrosternal pressure), generalized dyspnea. DURATION: Progressive over hours to days. CHARACTER: Dyspnea, chest pressure, feeling of impending doom. AGGRAVATING: Lying flat. RELIEVING: Sitting up, leaning forward. TIMING: Progressive worsening. SEVERITY: Severe respiratory distress. KEY POSITIVES: Beck's triad (hypotension, muffled heart sounds, JVD), pulsus paradoxus, tachycardia, dyspnea, recent pericarditis or trauma or malignancy. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT pleuritic pain, NOT unilateral symptoms.
